headline: Structured weights show an 8% drop (77.9 to 71.7 kg) from Sep 5 to Nov 24, 2026, but two notes say the Nov 24 weight-loss entry was a charting error, so the team needs to reconcile this. Separately, her son and primary caregiver Marcus reports exhaustion and has requested respite.

items.statement: The vitals record shows four weights falling steadily: 77.9 kg (Sep 5), 75.7 kg (Oct 1), 73.6 kg (Oct 28) and 71.7 kg (Nov 24). That is a 6.2 kg (13.7 lb), 8.0% loss. On Nov 27 and Nov 28, notes said the Nov 24 weight-loss entry was documented on the wrong participant and that Mariana had no such event; these notes do not explain the weight readings in her own vitals record.
items.verifier_note: The four weights, the 6.2 kg / 13.7 lb / 8.0% change, and the Nov 27 and Nov 28 correction notes all match the cited vitals record and notes. The notes address the Nov 24 weight-loss entry and say nothing about the vitals readings, so the statement that they do not explain those readings is accurate.

items.statement: On Sep 27, 2026 Marcus, her son and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone. He requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group. No later follow-up appears in the notes.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 27 note matches every detail: Marcus is the son and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion, poor sleep and worry about evenings alone, requested respite, and discussed respite options and a caregiver support group. The cited note contains no later follow-up, which is consistent with the closing sentence.

questions_for_team: Do the Sep 5 to Nov 24 weights in the vitals record belong to Mariana? Were they measured on her, or were they also misfiled? Can the weight be re-measured and the record corrected if needed?
If the weights are accurate, how does that fit with the chart correction saying no weight-loss event occurred? What should the team do about nutrition follow-up?
What respite options have been arranged for Marcus since Sep 27, and is the evening coverage gap resolved?
Has the caregiver support group referral been followed up?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and discharges, with reason for each.
Falls and fall-related injuries in the window; given osteoporosis, check for any fracture, new fall-risk medication, or near-falls documented.
Chest pain, angina episodes, and nitroglycerin spray use in the window (ischemic heart disease); check whether PRN nitroglycerin use has increased.
Blood pressure trend across the window (essential hypertension on metoprolol); flag any readings with systolic or diastolic outside the team's set thresholds, orthostatic symptoms, and dizziness.
Heart rate trend on metoprolol succinate; check for bradycardia or fatigue notes.

Diabetes and glycemic control: glucose and HbA1c results, hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia events, and whether any diabetes medication was started or changed (none appear on the active list; verify the list is complete).
Kidney function: eGFR, creatinine, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and potassium for CKD stage 1 with diabetic kidney disease; confirm any labs due in the window were completed.

Lipid panel and triglycerides (hypertriglyceridemia, metabolic syndrome, ischemic heart disease) against the simvastatin 20 mg regimen; check whether the statin dose or intensity has been reviewed and whether any statin-related muscle symptoms are documented.
Anemia and B12: hemoglobin and CBC trend, and vitamin B12 injection schedule and adherence, since she is on B12 injections; confirm the next dose is due or given.
Weight and BMI trend (BMI 30+ with metabolic syndrome); flag any unintentional weight change of concern and any dietary or activity referrals made.

Medication reconciliation: compare the active list (metoprolol, nitroglycerin, simvastatin, B12) against pharmacy fill history and any outside prescriptions; check for any starts, stops, or dose changes in the window, and confirm allergies, since the allergy list is empty and should be verified.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: any change in bathing, dressing, transfers, meal preparation, medication management, or driving, compared with the last review.
Cognition and mood: screening scores (e.g., MoCA/MMSE, PHQ-2/PHQ-9) and any new confusion, low mood, or social withdrawal documented in the window.
Caregiver and social situation: living arrangement changes, caregiver strain or availability, transportation barriers to PACE center attendance, and any housing or financial concerns.
Attendance at PACE center and day-program participation in the window; note missed days and reasons.

Care-plan items due: confirm due dates for the annual reassessment, bone density follow-up or osteoporosis treatment review, diabetic eye and foot exams, vaccinations, and any goals or interventions flagged as overdue.
Summarize findings as changes since last review for the IDT, with clear flags for items needing clinician decision rather than recommendations.
